title: PrivSec riff — control mapping + questions
content:
PrivSec riff — quick brain dump and control-mapping sketch (Kendall)

Context / intent:
- Lightweight personal notes to map out where our infra/security artifacts line up to typical AIC/AU/SOC2 control objectives. Not a finished doc — think: first pass, shorthand, questions to take to SRE/security sync.
- Primary focus: KMS/keys, SSO+SSO provisioning, long-term audit logs (ingest/retention), change control for serving-runtime, and evidence collection patterns for Dedicated/Private customers.

High-level control buckets (thinking aloud):
1) Identity & Access Management (provisioning, role reviews, MFA)
2) Crypto key management (KMS usage, rotation, separation of duties)
3) Logging & Monitoring (immutable logs, retention, access logs)
4) Change management & deployments (PR review, canary, rollbacks, approvals)
5) Data handling & segmentation (customer isolation for Dedicated/Private + data path docs)
6) Incident response & forensics (runbooks, evidence preservation)

Mapping sketch (very rough) — format: Control area -> Redwood artifact -> owner -> evidence pointer -> gaps
- IAM -> Okta + SCIM provisioning -> eng-plat (Rafael) -> OKTA-USER-AUDIT export / SCIM logs -> gap: scheduled role review cadence (who/when?)
- MFA enforcement -> Okta policy -> trust-ops (Asha) -> policy screenshot + system logs -> gap: MFA exceptions ledger (we have ad-hoc notes but not codified)
- KMS usage -> AWS KMS + customer KMS integration for Private -> infra-secrets (SRE) -> KMS key policy doc, CloudTrail KMS events -> gap: documented rotation proof for specific tenant keys (Dedicated)
- Log immutability -> ELK + S3 archival with WORM bucket policy -> observability (Jake) -> retention configs in terraform + s3 access logs -> gap: retention for customer-specific telemetry (how long for Private?)
- Service config change approvals -> GitHub PRs + CODEOWNERS -> release-eng -> merged PR history + release tags -> gap: formal approval stamp for config changes that affect customer dataflow (we rely on CODEOWNERS but auditors ask for explicit approval evidence)
- Deployment canary/fallback -> console rollouts + route policies -> product (Anjali) -> rollout history + automatic fallback alerts -> gap: exportable canary result artifacts for auditor review (need snapshot)

Evidence notes (what we can hand over quickly):
- PR history + signed commit SHAs (github) = good for change control, include related ticket numbers.
- CloudTrail + Okta logs = primary for IAM and KMS events, need curated time slices for auditor requests.
- Terraform state + module versions = shows declared state at point-in-time (useful for configuration).
- Console: rollout history CSV export (possible? ask product) — if not, take time-stamped screenshots + added commentary.

Open questions / discussion items (to bring to sync):
- Who will own the formal monthly role review (not just ad-hoc)? Proposal: trust-ops lead rotates with eng-plat monthly; escalate misses to Head of SRE.
- KMS rotation proof for Dedicated customers: do we generate a rotation certificate or export CloudTrail slices? Which is less intrusive?
- MFA exceptions: we currently allow exceptions via support tickets. Need a single ledger (maybe a simple sheet with TTL + approver). Who maintains? Security Ops?
- Backup/restore proof: auditors want to know restore exercises. We run restores ad-hoc — propose quarterly smoke restores for a sample datastore and a simple runbook and artifact (time-stamped logs + incident ticket).
- Private deployment evidence: customers expect proof of on-prem key separation + auditability. Draft checklist: KMS boundary diagram, KMS policy export, network ACL snapshot, console RBAC snapshot.

Quick wins (low lift):
- Add a single canonical ledger (Google Sheet) for MFA exceptions and role review outcomes. Owner: trust-ops. Column headers: user, role, exception-reason, approver, expiry, ticket-ref.
- Create a one-click archive script to export CloudTrail slices (by time range and event filter) to an evidence bucket. Put run instructions in a playbook. Owner: infra-secrets.
- Add a Governance tag to PR titles that touch config files controlling data flows (README, routing, kv-cache). That makes later evidence pulls easy.

Longer-term / medium lift:
- Build an Evidence Pack generator: given a date range + ticket set, assemble PR SHAs, CloudTrail slices, Okta audit logs, deployment tags into a zip. Could be part of Redwood Console Optimize (export for audits).
- Formalize cadence for role reviews + retention policy doc for customer-specific telemetry.

Meeting agenda for next sync (10–15m):
- Walk this mapping (5m)
- Decide role-review owner + cadence (3m)
- Approve low-lift items and owners (2m)
- Assign one experiment: CloudTrail export script (2–3w owner Rafael)

Random notes / reminders to self:
- When pulling CloudTrail for KMS, filter eventName: "GenerateDataKey" "Encrypt" "ReEncrypt" "CreateKey". Timestamp timezone: include UTC.
- For Okta exports use System Log API -> good to include actor IP and userAgent.
- Evidence must be time-bound: include 'pulled_at' timestamp on every artifact.
- Keep copies (hash) of exported evidence in a locked bucket and a ticket reference.

Draft messaging for CS (short):
"Working on a compact evidence playbook for audit/attestation requests. Short term: we can provide PR history, KMS CloudTrail slices, Okta audit logs and a deployment snapshot. Will share a one-sheet with steps to request a package."

Next actions (as TODOs):
- [ ] Rafael: prototype CloudTrail export script + example output (due 2026-03-15)
- [ ] Asha: create MFA exception ledger + seed with current exceptions (due 2026-03-12)
- [ ] Me (Kendall): draft one-page evidence playbook and sample request form (due 2026-03-10) — include 'pulled_at' hash guidance
- [ ] Product: confirm if Console can export rollout history (ask Anjali)

Footer: this is a riff — prune and move to Confluence once we have consensus. Keep it terse and actionable.
